parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

**HealthyMunch **

HealthyMunch is a social enterprise based in Country Z that provides nutritious, affordable meals to elderly and vulnerable people. Founded 5 years ago, HealthyMunch now serves over 500 customers daily through its meal delivery service and two community cafes.

As a social enterprise, HealthyMunch reinvests all profits into expanding its services and improving meal quality. Last year, it had revenue of \$750,000 and made a profit of \$50,000. The company employs 30 full-time staff and works with 50 volunteers.

HealthyMunch markets its services through a mix of traditional and digital methods. They distribute brochures in local community centers and doctor's offices, and have partnerships with local health services for referrals. Their social media presence focuses on sharing nutritional tips and customer testimonials. They also rely heavily on word-of-mouth recommendations from satisfied customers and their families.

To better understand its market, HealthyMunch conducts regular market research. They use a combination of surveys, focus groups, and analysis of customer order data. Recent findings show that there's growing demand for specialized diets (e.g., low-sodium, diabetic-friendly meals) and interest in cooking classes for family caregivers. They've also identified a potential new market segment of busy working adults looking for healthy, ready-made meals.

HealthyMunch is considering expanding its services to include nutrition education programs in local schools. This would require hiring specialised staff and developing new educational materials. The company estimates this expansion would cost \$100,000 initially but could increase revenue by 20% within two years.

However, HealthyMunch faces some challenges. Food costs have risen by 15% in the past year due to inflation, putting pressure on its margins. The company is also experiencing increased competition from for-profit meal delivery services targeting the elderly.

The board of directors is divided on whether to pursue the school program expansion or focus on improving efficiency in its current operations. They need to make a decision soon, as government grants for school nutrition programs will be available in 3 months.

HealthyMunch prides itself on its strong relationships with customers and the local community. It regularly conducts surveys to gather feedback and has a customer satisfaction rating of 92%. 

**Appendix 1: HealthyMunch Financial Data**

| **Year** | **Revenue (\$000)** | **Profit (\$000)** | **Number of meals served daily** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2022 | 750 | 50 | 500 |
| 2021 | 650 | 45 | 450 |
| 2020 | 550 | 35 | 400 |

Consider how the following three factors could affect HealthyMunch's marketing strategy.

- Changing customer needs
- Increased competition
- Use of market segmentation

Which factor is likely to have the greatest impact on HealthyMunch's future success? Justify your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/10/healthymunch-case-study.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
Changing customer needs are evident in HealthyMunch's market research. There's growing demand for specialised diets and interest in cooking classes for family carers **[Ap]**. This could be both an opportunity and a challenge for HealthyMunch to adapt its products to meet these changing needs **[An]**

Increased competition is a concern, with for-profit meal delivery services now targeting the elderly market **[Ap]**. This could reduce HealthyMunch's market share and may mean it has to reduce prices to maintain sales **[An]**. The company should consider emphasising its social enterprise status **[Ap] **and community work to differentiate itself from these new rivals **[An]**

HealthMunch already uses market segmentation as it targets elderly and vulnerable people **[Ap]**. It could look at targeting other market segments, such as busy working adults seeking healthy, ready-made meals **[Ap]. **This could reduce the impact of increased competition in their original target market **[An]**

While all three factors are important, changing customer needs are likely to have the greatest impact on HealthyMunch's success **[E]**. By matching meals to customer preferences, such as specialised diets and nutrition education **[Ap]**, HealthyMunch can strengthen customer loyalty and potentially expand its customer base **[E]**. This focus on meeting changing needs will also help the company stay ahead of the growing number of competitors **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Changing customer needs**
> 
>   - Growing demand for specialized diets (low-sodium, diabetic-friendly) → marketing must spotlight tailored meal plans and health benefits
>   - Rising interest in cooking classes for caregivers → opportunity to promote educational services alongside meals
>   - Emerging segment of busy working adults seeking healthy ready-made meals → calls for digital convenience messaging and targeted online ads
> - **Increased competition**
> 
>   - Entry of for-profit meal services targeting the elderly → forces repositioning around social-enterprise mission and reinvestment of profits
>   - Higher food-cost inflation (15%) → squeezes margins vs competitors → marketing must emphasize value and quality
>   - Limited grant window for school programs → competitors may capture funding → need urgent, compelling campaign to secure support
> - **Use of market segmentation**
> 
>   - Dietary-need segments → craft distinct promotions for low-sodium vs diabetic vs general-health plans
>   - Demographic segments (elderly, caregivers, busy adults) → choose appropriate channels: brochures in clinics, caregiver groups, social media
>   - Service segments (meal delivery, community café, education programs) → develop bespoke messaging and cross-sell tactics
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Changing customer needs will have the greatest impact, as adapting menu offerings and messaging to specific dietary and lifestyle trends is essential to retain existing clients and win new segments
>   - Competition demands a strong, value-led positioning but relies on meeting customer needs first
>   - Segmentation enables precise targeting but is only effective once customer needs are clearly understood and addressed

**Extract:**

{align=center} **Everyone Theatre (ET) **

Zane and Zaara are both actors. They plan to start up a theatre in a low-income area of Main City. Zane and Zaara believe that helping the community is as important as being successful entrepreneurs. 

The theatre will be a private sector business and Zane and Zaara have to decide whether to start up as an unincorporated business (partnership) or as a limited company. Zane is planning to prepare a cash-flow forecast for the first year. Zaara knows they will need to set business objectives for the theatre and also decide on a leadership style to use when managing employees. ET will have 24 part-time employees as shown in the organisational chart in Appendix 1. 

Zane and Zaara plan to put on performances in the evenings for local people and tourists. There will be 100 seats in the theatre but not all the seats will be sold if the price is too high. The Marketing Manager, Zaara, will need to decide which performances to put on, what price to charge and which refreshments to sell. Zaara will also need to decide between the two possible options for the first performance when the theatre opens. Information on the two options is shown in Appendix 2. 

In the daytime the theatre building will be used by Daycare, a local social enterprise. Daycare takes care of young children up to the age of 5 so that low-income family members can go out to work. It also provides education for the children which helps their development and progress before they start school. Some of Daycare’s objectives are different to those of ET.

{align=center}

{align=center}

| Average wage cost per actor/employee | \$30 | \$10 |
| All other costs including scenery, costumes and promotion | \$1000 | \$2000 |

{align=center} **Appendix 3 **

{align=center} **Email from Zane to Zaara**

To: Zaara

We want to support the local community and we need to make decisions about the following.

Should we:

- Pay fair wages even though they may be higher than those paid by competing theatres?
- Only buy costumes produced in the local community?
- Purchase all refreshments from suppliers that do not pollute the environment?

Consider the following three roles of marketing for ET.

- Identifying customer needs
- Satisfying customer needs
- Maintaining customer loyalty

Which role will be the most important for ET to be successful? Justify your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/jun-2023-paper-2-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
As a new theatre in a low-income area **[Ap]**, ET must understand what types of performances and prices appeal to local people and tourists, so that it can fill seats. For example, they need to research if audiences prefer comedies, musicals or dramas **[Ap]**. This helps ET plan performances that attract enough customers to buy tickets and bring in revenue **[An]**. Zaara must also determine the price customers are willing to pay. If ticket prices are too high, many seats may remain empty, leading to a loss **[An]**

While satisfying customer needs is important to build ET's reputation and encourage customers to recommend the new theatre **[Ap] **to others, they can't satisfy needs they haven't identified first **[An]**. Maintaining loyalty is less crucial initially, as ET will likely attract different audiences like tourists **[Ap], **though it will be important as the theatre becomes established to ensure regular income **[An]**. However, without first identifying needs, ET risks putting on performances **[Ap]** that. don't appeal to customers, so don't sell many tickets. This could lead to financial losses and damage their ability to stay open **[An]**

ET needs to consider all three roles of marketing, but identifying customer needs is probably the most important for success **[E]**. By focusing on identifying customers' entertainment needs, ET can make informed decisions about performances, pricing and refreshments, giving them the best chance of attracting loyal audiences **[Ap]**, generating revenue and becoming a successful theatre **[E]** that serves its community **[Ap]**

parts.problem_md: Do you think entering a growing market where there is a lot of competition is the best way for a business to expand? Justify your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Entering a growing market with lots of competition can allow a business to take advantage of high potential demand** [K]**, which could lead to increased revenue. However, with many competitors, it's hard for a business to make its product stand out unless it lowers prices. As customers may already be loyal to other brands, it can be difficult to gain market share. This could result in lower growth than expected **[An]**

Instead, a business could develop new products for its existing market or find a new market with less competition **[K]**.  This might provide a chance for higher profits as there is less pressure on prices, which could then provide the finance necessary to fund growth **[An]**

Overall, although entering a growing market is likely to be risky, if a business can take advantage of growing sales without spending too much on promotional activity or price cuts, it is an effective way to achieve growth **[E]**. Whether it is always the best method, however, is less clear** [E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Shows high potential demand/many potential customers [k] could lead to an increase in revenue [an]
>   - Have to do something different to make your product ‘stand out’/ customers may be brand loyal to other businesses/ more choice [k] leading to higher/lower sales [an] leading to higher/lower revenue [an]
>   - Allow the business to spread risk [k]
>   - Difficult to charge high prices/may have to set lower prices (than competitors) [k] lowering the profit margin/so difficult to break-even [an]
>   - (Additional) costs of promotion/market research [k] leading to higher expenses [an]
>   - Makes the business be more efficient [k] to reduce average costs [an]
> - Other options might include:
> 
>   - Develop new products [k]
>   - Expand in existing market [k]
>   - Find new market with low/no competition [k] provides chance for monopoly (as no competition) [an]
>   - Take over a competitor [k] so gain their market share [an]
> - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - A growing market shows high potential demand [k] so possible to earn enough revenue to recover costs [an]. However, if there is a lot of competition then it might be difficult to charge high prices [k] and this might lower the profit margin [an] which could make it difficult to recover the cost of developing new products [an]. It will depend on how good its product is because if customers are interested in what the business is offering, they may be prepared to buy it despite the competition so in this situation it is worth the risk as they would be able to gain market share to justify the costs of expansion.[eval] [eval]
> - Some points can be awarded as either [k] or [an] but only allow once
> - For evaluation to be awarded, justification will usually follow on from relevant analysis of points

parts.problem_md: Do you think maintaining customer loyalty should be more important to a business than attracting new customers? Justify your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Existing loyal customers can provide free advertising by recommending the product to others **[K]**. This spreads positive word-of-mouth and helps maintain the company's reputation, giving it a competitive advantage **[An]**

However, attracting new customers can widen the target market **[K]** and increase revenue. As customer tastes change, it may be cheaper to find new customers than develop new products for existing ones **[An]**

Overall, customer loyalty is more important than attracting new customers for most businesses **[E]**. While new customers can increase market share, loyal customers provide stable revenue and free advertising, which can enhance a business's reputation. Businesses should focus on retaining current customers while still seeking new ones when possible **[E]**

parts.problem_md: Explain two ways a retail business could respond to increased competition. Which would be the best way to use? Justify your answer.
parts.solution_md:
A retail business could respond to increased competition by lowering its prices **[K]**. This may help sell more products in its store and increase market share, potentially boosting revenue. However, it might also reduce profit margins **[An]**

Secondly, the business could introduce new products **[K]**. This could give the shop a unique selling point and appeal to a wider range of customers, but it may be limited by available shelf space **[An]**

Introducing new products would be the best way to respond **[E]**. While lowering prices might attract some customers, it could start a price war and harm profits. New products, on the other hand, could help the business stand out from competitors. It might attract new customers without necessarily reducing profits. This strategy could lead to increased sales and customer loyalty, making it a more sustainable long-term solution to increased competition **[E]**

>   - Maintain/build good customer relationships [k] which could encourage customer loyalty [an]

When Pamela started her business 30 years ago she had no help to manage the shop. She now has 5 employees. Pamela knows maintaining customer loyalty is important. She uses competitive pricing. Most of her marketing budget is spent on sales promotion. Pamela does not use e-commerce.
parts.solution_md:
Pamela could start a loyalty scheme **[K]** using her marketing budget. For example, customers could get a stamp each time they buy something, and after 10 stamps they get a free card or small toy **[Ap]**. This would give customers a reason to keep coming back to Pamela's shop instead of going elsewhere **[An]**

Pamela could train her 5 employees to provide excellent customer service **[K]**. They could learn how to greet customers warmly, help them find the perfect gift **[Ap]**, and handle any complaints quickly. Good service is especially important for a gift shop selling celebration items, as customers want to feel happy and excited about their purchases. When customers have a good experience in the shop, they are more likely to return **[An]**

parts.problem_md: Do you think offering good customer service is the best way for a small business to build customer relationships? Justify your answer.

Offering good customer service can be an effective way for a small business to build customer relationships **[K]**. It may require training for employees, which increases costs for a small business, but it makes customers feel valued, which can improve loyalty as it builds trust and enhances the business's reputation **[An]**

Other options, like loyalty schemes and conducting market research **[K]**, can encourage repeat purchases and help a business understand its customers. Both of these could improve customer relationships but, similarly, incur costs, which may be difficult for a small business to justify **[An]**

Overall, I think good customer service is the best approach for a small business **[E]**.** **While there are some costs involved, it directly impacts the customer experience and can attract new customers through positive word-of-mouth. This can increase revenue to offset staff training costs. It also doesn't require as much upfront investment as options like loyalty programmes, making it more suitable for a small business with limited resources **[E]**

Having only one customer can be risky for a business. If that customer does not buy **[K]**, the business could quickly fail due to cash flow issues, as they do not have other sources of revenue to cover costs **[An]**

However, the business can focus  on the needs of that customer **[K]**, potentially increasing loyalty. It may also incur significantly lower marketing costs, as there is no need to attract new customers **[An]**

Overall, the risks of having just one customer are too high, as the business ties its success to just one other business over which it has little control **[E]**.That business, for example, has a lot of power to influence prices, as without it, a business would be in significant financial trouble. Therefore, it is better to have a wider customer base for more stability and independence **[E]**

parts.problem_md: Do you think operating in a niche market will help a small business have a better chance of success than operating in a mass market? Justify your answer.
parts.solution_md:
In a niche market, a business can focus closely on customer's needs **[K]**,  which has a good chance of leading to customer loyalty. This allows the business to build strong relationships with customers and understand their specific requirements **[An]**

While mass markets have more potential customers, they also face increased competition **[K]**. This can make it harder for small businesses to stand out. However, niche markets have drawbacks too. They offer less potential for growth and may be vulnerable to changes in consumer spending patterns **[An]**

For a small business starting out, the benefits of operating in a niche market likely outweigh the drawbacks **[E]**.With loyal customers, businesses can set higher prices for their specialised products. This can lead to higher profit margins, especially important for small businesses with limited resources **[E]**

>     - May be able to set higher prices (for a high status, exclusive product) [k] so able to have high / increase profit margin [an]

>

In a mass market, there are more potential customers [k] which could mean higher revenue [an]. However, I do think a small business has a better chance of success in a niche market because it can continue to charge high prices [eval] as large companies will not see the market as worthwhile because of potentially low sales. [eval]

parts.problem_md:
Explain **one **advantage and **one **disadvantage to Elton of operating in a niche market.

> **[case-study]**
> Elton is a sole trader. He sells specialist clothing and equipment for sports, including baseball and hockey. It is a niche market. Elton started his business 5 years ago and it has remained small. A wide range of inventory is important. Elton has been looking at the financial performance of his business. The profit margin for 2018 was 35%. An extract of the accounts is shown in the below table.
> 
> | **Revenue and cost information for Elton’s business for 2018 and 2019 (\$)** |   |   |
> |---|---|---|
> |   | **2018** | **2019** |
> | Revenue (\$) | 24 000 | 25 000 |
> | Cost of sales (\$) | 7 200 | **Y** |
> | Gross profit (\$) | 16 800 | 18 000 |
> | Expenses (\$) | 8 400 | 10 000 |
> | Profit (\$) | **X** | 8 000 |
parts.solution_md:
One advantage to Elton of operating in a niche market is that he can charge higher prices **[K] **for his specialist sports clothing and equipment. This helps explain why his profit margin is 35%, which is quite high **[Ap]**. Customers interested in baseball and hockey gear are often willing to pay more for expert products and advice. This allows Elton to maintain good profitability despite being a small business **[An]**

However, Elton needs to stock a wide range of stock **[K]**. Having to offer many different items of specialist clothing and equipment for sports like baseball and hockey **[Ap]** means Elton probably can't benefit from bulk-buying discounts. This could make it harder for him to reduce his costs and grow the business beyond its current small size, even after 5 years of operation **[An]**

**Examiner tips**

- You do not need to include definitions of key terms in six-mark 'explain' questions, as knowledge marks are awarded for stating valid points

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Write two developed paragraphs, one for each part of the question
> - For each paragraph:
> 
>   - State a valid point relevant to the question → 1 K mark
>   - Apply it clearly to the business in the case study → 1 Ap mark
>   - Explain the impact using a cause–effect chain → 1 An mark
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Advantages:
>   
>     - Less competition [k] so easier to attract/retain customers [an] to his shop [app]
>     - Clear focus/easier to target customers [k] interested in certain sports [app] reducing costs of advertising [an]
>     - Builds up specialist skills and knowledge [k]
>     - Can often charge a higher price [k] helps improve profit margin [an]
>     - Customers are prepared to pay for expertise [k]
>     - Customers tend to be more loyal [k] so may remain in business for another 5 years [app]
>   - Disadvantages:
>   
>     - Lack of economies of scale [k] leading to higher unit costs [an] so not able to lower cost of sales of \$7000 [app]
>     - Risk of over dependence on a single product or market [k]
>     - Likely to attract competition if successful [k]
>     - Vulnerable to market changes [k]
>   - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
> - Application
> 
>   - To use words from the stem as application, the reference must be appropriate (i.e. make sense) in relation to the point being made
>   - The following words are likely to be appropriate for this question:
>   
>     - Sole trader
>     - 5 years
>     - Clothing and equipment for sports
>     - shop
>     - Remained small
>     - Wide range of inventory needed
>     - Profit margin was 35%
>     - Use of figures from Table 3.1
>   - Other appropriate examples in context can still be credited
>   - Candidates may gain credit for changes to profit margin only once in either the advantage OR the disadvantage

parts.problem_md: Do you think that more advertising is a better way for a business to respond to increased competition than introducing new products and services? Justify your answer.
parts.solution_md:
While more advertising can raise awareness of products **[K]**, which may increase revenue, it can be expensive and doesn't guarantee sales will rise, especially if competitors also engage in advertising their own products **[An]**

Introducing new products allows a business to appeal to more potential customers **[K] **with new goods or services that could be more appealing than those of rivals. Although product development is also potentially very costly, it can help spread risk and increase potential sales, some of which may be taken from competitors **[An]**

Overall, introducing new products is likely better as it allows the business to adapt to changing customer needs** [E]**. While advertising existing products may provide a short-term boost, new products that truly meet customer wants are more likely to provide a sustained competitive advantage in the long run, allowing a business to raise prices and increase revenue **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Advertising:
>   
>     - To raise awareness of its products [k] to increase revenue [an] but products might not be what customers want which will limit effectiveness [an]
>     - No guarantee that target customers may see it [k] so sales may not rise [an]
>     - More advertising will increase costs [k]
>     - Widen target market/appeal to more potential customers [k]
>   - Introducing new products:
>   
>     - Widen target market/appeal to more potential customers [k]
>     - May not appeal to customers [k]
>     - High cost of development [k] which will add to expenses [an]
>     - Allows access to new markets [k] which helps spread risk [an] and increases potential sales [an]
>   - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
>   - For evaluation to be awarded justification will usually follow on from relevant analysis of points
>   - For the second evaluation mark the candidate must address that there is increased competition

The mass market is a very large number of customers** [K] **to whom businesses sell an undifferentiated product **[K]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure your answer specifically defines the mass market rather than a market more generally

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 2
> 
>   - Give a clearly-stated, valid definition to achieve both knowledge [K] marks
>   - 2 marks for a full definition, 1 mark for a partial definition
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Selling** the same** product (1) to the whole market. (1)
